page: Microsoft Azure E8-2s_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance based on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. The instance features a dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 2 vCPUs provisioned across 1 physical core with 2 threads per core. Cache resources include 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and access to 260 MB of L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX-512 and Intel AMX matrix acceleration, alongside hardware cryptography capabilities such as AES and SHA extensions.

The instance provides 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high ratio of 32.0 GB of memory per core. No dedicated graphics processing units are present, and the instance includes no local storage, requiring attached remote storage volumes for persistent data. Additionally, it provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-threaded performance, recording a Geekbench single-core score of 2147.0 and single-threaded gzip compression at 31.33 GB/sec. However, due to its constrained configuration of a single physical core, multi-core throughput remains restricted, yielding a Geekbench multi-core score of 2632.0 and a multi-core stress-ng score of 1992.38. Uncached memory bandwidth reaches 21.05 GB/sec for large reads and 14.27 GB/sec for large writes, reflecting constrained throughput under sustained uncached memory access.

From a resource allocation standpoint, the E8-2s_v6 trades raw compute parallelization for high memory density. This design suits workloads requiring substantial in-memory footprints with minimal concurrent CPU requirements, such as small in-memory caches, light database instances, memory-heavy batch workers, or background analytical jobs where licensing favors low core counts.

The instance lacks local storage and GPU accelerators, relying entirely on remote storage volumes. Benchmark metrics highlight strong single-core capabilities, achieving a Geekbench single-core score of 2147.0 and rapid gzip compression of 31.33 GB/sec.
